body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. The control imported a native vertical punch and plotted its rough cut and trims. Separate CAMCraft CLI tests on this PR verified that omitting the taper, setting it to zero, and clearing an existing taper produced identical vertical NC. The control did not exercise the command parser.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 79b4d4339a56067e7e8e4e0310a722fbc385018b -->
Review at head 79b4d4339. Read, not built: the PR is from a fork, so its code does not run on the maintainer's runners, and no local build slot was free. The author's quick gate (17/17) and reached heavy gate (199/199) passed on macOS arm64 at this head.

The change reads well:
- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`: the project DTO drops a zero `taper_deg` on the read-back, so `lost()` refused an explicit return to vertical. The fix seeds `back["taper_deg"]` from the typed `next` value for WireContour only. The typed value is what the operation holds, so the check is stronger, not weaker.
- I traced the edges: a misspelled key still fails (the seed adds only `taper_deg`, so `lost()` still finds the misspelled path); a taper patch on another kind still fails (the seed is WireContour-only); `taper_deg: null` still removes and passes, because `lost()` skips null patch values before it consults `back`.
- The new test pins all four cases at 79b4d4339: add with `0`, edit 3 degrees, edit back to `0.0` (with the saved form asserted to omit the key), the misspelling, and the wrong-kind refusal. The fixture `edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch` is in the tree.
- File sizes: `edit.rs` 392 lines, `mcp_wire_contour.rs` 233 lines. No process file changes. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2925`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/2925-wire-zero-taper.md` explains why the fix stays narrow.

Clean. Label: merge-ready. Note for the merge batch: the check guards values that reach a posted wire path, so a safety-tier second read before the merge fits the rule for posted G-code.
